report.source_text: Symptoms improved gradually after two weeks of IV antibiotics, specifically Unasyn, administered at a standard dose of 3 g every six hours. Following this, he was discharged with a six-week course of the oral 𝛃-lactam antibiotic, amoxicillin-clavulanate, at a dosage of 500 mg/125 mg three times a day. Repeat CT of the abdomen 10 weeks after presentation showed complete resolution of the hepatic abscesses.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Pyogenic liver abscess due to Fusobacterium species
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 26-year-old male presented with 3-week progressive febrile illness, sepsis, right upper quadrant pain, dyspnea, and pleuritic chest pain. Imaging confirmed a large liver abscess (3.9×4.4×3.5 cm). CT-guided percutaneous drainage was performed with drain placement. Aspirate cultures grew Fusobacterium species while blood cultures remained negative, prompting targeted antibiotic therapy with ampicillin-sulbactam. The hospital course was complicated by portal vein thrombosis, recurrent pleural effusions requiring multiple thoracenteses (accounting for respiratory symptoms), and biliary fistula formation requiring ERCP with sphincterotomy and stent placement. Investigation for a primary source revealed good oral hygiene and no recent dental procedures. Following 2 weeks of IV ampicillin-sulbactam and 6 weeks of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate, repeat CT at 10 weeks demonstrated complete resolution of the hepatic abscesses.
